title: The container return experiment
paragraphs: At Taman Sari riverside market, takeaway meals were usually served in disposable bowls. The vendors' association wanted to test a reusable alternative without slowing the busy evening service. For four consecutive Fridays, six food stalls shared 120 sturdy containers. Customers paid a small refundable deposit and received a wooden token when they returned a container.

During the first Friday, many customers carried used containers back to the stall where they had bought their meal. The narrow queues made serving difficult. Before the second Friday, volunteers moved the collection point beside the bus exit and added picture signs in three languages. The return rate rose from 62 per cent on the first night to an average of 86 per cent across the next three Fridays. Because both changes were introduced together, the records could not show how much each one contributed.

Some vendors had worried that washing containers would delay orders. Instead, volunteers took the used containers to a community kitchen after the market closed, while a clean spare set was delivered before the next opening. Observers sampled service times at ten-minute intervals and found that the median waiting time at participating stalls did not increase. However, their observations did not include the annual festival night, when the market is unusually crowded.

By the fourth Friday, the six participating stalls were buying fewer disposable bowls than they had bought before the trial. Their nearby waste bins were also lighter at closing time. Yet two trial evenings were rainy and attracted fewer visitors, and the market's other stalls continued using disposable packaging. The association therefore did not claim that the experiment had reduced total waste across the whole market.

The association extended the experiment for another six weeks. It planned to record hourly visitor numbers and the number of containers issued, and to ask customers who kept a container why they had not returned it. Two additional vendors joined after reading the service-time observations. The town council said it would consider funding a permanent washing station only after reviewing the longer trial.
